turn_text: I think so many of us are wondering what it ultimately is going to take. And I think many people within the Democratic Party aren't happy with some of the more extreme aspects in the Republican Party. I think a lot of people are extremely nervous about the more extreme aspects. What is it going to take to bring people back, bring this country together, bring individuals within parties together? What would you do to do that, Secretary Clinton?

Well, I think that because this is such a consequential campaign, we have to look and ask ourselves, and I hope, you know, the voters in Utah will do this. You know, what do we need from our next president? Because somebody's going to walk into that Oval Office next January. I think there are three big tests that are awaiting whoever that person is. Can you make positive differences in people's lives? Can you give people You know, not just the hope, but the reality that their hard work will be rewarded if they can get ahead and stay ahead. Can you keep us safe here at home and maintain American leadership around the world? We are living in a very complex world. There's a lot of opportunity, but there are also a lot of threats. So what do we expect from the person in that Oval Office? And then finally, can we bring our country together? All this divisiveness is separating us between different groups. To be great, we can't be small. We can't lose what made America great in the first place. And so I really believe that people will view this more as a job interview.
